symbols.H: the hypothesis space: the set of hypotheses the learner can choose from
symbols.epsilon: the error goal: how much true error we accept (in agnostic learning, the allowed gap to training error)
symbols.h: a hypothesis: one candidate classifier the learner could output
symbols.m: the number of training examples (or of points, when testing shattering)
symbols.delta: the allowed chance of failure: the sample may be unlucky with probability at most this
symbols.e: the base of the exponential (about 2.718) in the bounds
symbols.C: the class of possible target concepts; inside VC, the C of the name VC
symbols.V: the V in VC (VC dimension) or in VS (version space), part of the name
symbols.n: the length of an instance (number of variables)
symbols.cal:D: the fixed, unknown probability distribution that instances are drawn from
symbols.ln: the natural logarithm of the quantity that follows
symbols.r: in the version-space diagram, the training error
symbols.d: the VC dimension (how many points can be shattered); in the linear rule, the number of features
symbols.c: the target concept: the true rule that gives each instance's correct label
symbols.x: an instance: one example's input (a single number in the threshold and interval examples)
symbols.D: the training set: the examples the learner sees (not the distribution)
symbols.S: the set of points tested for shattering; in VS, the S of the name
symbols.theta: a parameter the classifier tunes, usually a threshold (on one slide, the whole parameter vector)
symbols.in: is an element of, or belongs to
symbols.X: the instance space: the set of all possible instances
symbols.bf:x: an instance as a vector: its list of attribute or feature values
symbols.k: counts attributes or labels a hypothesis (h_k); in the proof, the number of bad hypotheses
symbols.t: in the singleton class [x = t], the one special point
symbols.g: the g in the more-general-than symbol: one hypothesis accepts at least what another accepts
symbols.j: labels or counts hypotheses, as in h_j
symbols.y: the label given to a point
symbols.bb:R: the real numbers: any number on the number line
symbols.log: the logarithm of the quantity that follows (base 2 in the VC bound)
symbols.Pr: the probability of the event in the brackets
symbols.abs: the number of elements in the set between the bars (|H| is the size of H)
symbols.alpha: the one parameter of the sine classifier: its frequency
symbols.v: the number of values attribute i can take
symbols.b: the right end of the interval [a, b]
symbols.w: the weights of a linear classifier: how much each feature counts
symbols.a: the left end of the interval [a, b]
symbols.prod: multiply together the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.L: the learner: the algorithm that picks a hypothesis from the data
symbols.f: a classifier as a function: it maps a point to a label
symbols.infty: infinity; VC dimension of infinity means arbitrarily large sets can be shattered
symbols.I: the indicator: 1 when the condition inside is true, otherwise 0
symbols.mid: such that: the set contains hypotheses that satisfy the condition on the right
symbols.w:sign: the sign function: positive score gives +1 and negative gives -1
symbols.T: the transpose: turns a column of numbers into a row
symbols.gamma: the margin of a separable dataset, used in the perceptron mistake bound
symbols.R: the largest length of any instance, in the perceptron mistake bound
symbols.max: the largest value of the term that follows, over the values shown
symbols.norm: the length of the vector inside
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.w:not: negation: the event that the version space is not exhausted
symbols.w:error: a hypothesis's error rate: calligraphic D subscript is true error, plain D is training error
symbols.w:best: h_best: the hypothesis with the fewest training errors
symbols.w:size: size(c): the encoding length of the target concept
symbols.w:consistent: Consistent(h, D): h gives the right label on every training example

The big picture.epsilon: the error goal: how much true error we accept
The big picture.e: the base of the exponential in the bound

Setup, true error.C: the set of possible target concepts
Setup, true error.D: the sequence of training examples the learner sees

PAC learning.C: the set of possible target concepts
PAC learning.n: the length of an instance, which resources may only grow polynomially with
PAC learning.c: the target concept (and size(c) is its encoding length)

Concept learning and EnjoySport.k: labels a hypothesis (h_k), or counts attributes in the formulas
Concept learning and EnjoySport.v: the number of values attribute i can take

Version spaces.S: the S of VS (version space), or the specific boundary in the figure
Version spaces.r: the training error of a hypothesis in the figure
Version spaces.D: the training set that hypotheses must be consistent with

Sample complexity for finite.e: the base of the exponential e^(-epsilon m)
Sample complexity for finite.k: the number of bad hypotheses (true error at least epsilon)
Sample complexity for finite.epsilon: the error goal: the most true error we accept
Sample complexity for finite.H: the finite hypothesis space; |H| is how many hypotheses it has

Agnostic PAC learning.epsilon: the gap we allow between true error and training error
Agnostic PAC learning.e: the base of the exponential in e^(-2m epsilon squared)
Agnostic PAC learning.D: the training set: error_D is training error
Agnostic PAC learning.h: a hypothesis; h_best is the one with fewest training errors

Infinite hypothesis.abs: the number of elements of the set: |X| counts instances
Infinite hypothesis.H: the hypothesis space, here possibly infinite

Shattering.S: the set of points we try to label every possible way
Shattering.f: a classifier that maps a point to a label
Shattering.theta: the classifier's parameters: some value of them gets zero training error
Shattering.T: the transpose, as in the dot product of x with itself
Shattering.y: the label we try to give a point
Shattering.m: the number of points; there are 2^m ways to label them

VC dimension and number.alpha: the single frequency parameter of the sine classifier
VC dimension and number.I: the indicator: 1 when the sine is positive, otherwise 0
VC dimension and number.theta: one of the 100 threshold parameters; only their sum matters

Sample complexity from VC.alpha: the single frequency parameter of the sine classifier
Sample complexity from VC.d: the VC dimension of a finite H, at most log base 2 of |H|
Sample complexity from VC.log: the base-2 logarithm in the VC bound
Sample complexity from VC.I: the indicator: 1 when the sine is positive, otherwise 0

Mentioned elsewhere.gamma: the margin of the separable data
Mentioned elsewhere.R: the largest length of any training instance
Mentioned elsewhere.max: the largest value over all instances i

Worked examples.epsilon: the error goal; in the agnostic example, the allowed gap
Worked examples.alpha: the sine classifier's frequency, built to fit chosen labels
Worked examples.w: a weight of a linear classifier
Worked examples.i: counts attributes, points or labels in the example
Worked examples.k: counts attributes with their value counts

Formula sheet.n: the instance length that resources may only grow polynomially with
Formula sheet.k: labels a hypothesis (h_k) in the generality order
Formula sheet.i: counts attributes in the hypothesis-count products
Formula sheet.v: the number of values attribute i can take
Formula sheet.d: the number of features in the linear rule d + 1; the VC dimension elsewhere
Formula sheet.epsilon: the error goal; in the agnostic rows, the gap between true and training error
Formula sheet.e: the base of the exponential in the bounds
Formula sheet.D: the training set (in VS) or its error (error_D)

Exam traps.d: the number of features in d + 1; or the VC dimension in the bound with log base 2
Exam traps.epsilon: the error goal; in the agnostic bound, the gap
Exam traps.delta: the failure probability: 95% confidence means delta of 0.05
